live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: detachFunc frees the auxiliary btree and schema in attach.c while a TEMP TRIGGER in aDb[1] keeps pTabSchema pointing at it, and sqlite3DropTriggerPtr -> tableOfTrigger reads pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash in trigger.c. Fixed upstream in 3.30.0

fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Built in the coreT group (-USQLITE_OMIT_TEMPDB): without a temp database the trigger has nowhere to survive

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect

fault_sites_why: PROVENANCE.md names the chain that reads the freed auxiliary schema: sqlite3DropTriggerPtr -> tableOfTrigger -> sqlite3HashFind(&pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash, ...). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. host ASan (results/2026-10-11-host-asan, shared/run-host-asan.py: every SQLite object its own malloc) reports the heap-use-after-free in findElementWithHash, which sqlite3HashFind calls with &pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash: tableOfTrigger only forms that address, the first load from the freed schema is pH->ht. Added 2026-10-11. The Sublet run 09a9cbc9 faulted there first and read NO-READING against the sites above; this entry rests on the ASan report, which is independent of it.
